issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 of the proof of Proposition 4.4, stationarity of a non-stationary point \underline{\tensX} is violated when at least one of the two optimality conditions is non-zero. If the first term \|\nabla f(\underline{\tensX}) \times_{k \in [d]\setminus I} \proj_{\underline{\matu}_k}\|_\frob^2 = 0 while the second term is strictly positive, the minimum \bar{\delta}(\underline{\tensX}) equals 0, leading to \delta(\underline{\tensX}) = 0. Consequently, the guaranteed decrease becomes non-strict (f(\tensY) - f(\tensX) \leq 0), defeating the contradiction in Theorem 4.5. Moreover, the case split on whether \|\nabla f(\tensX_{\underline{\vecr}}) \times_{k \in I} \dots\| is zero or non-zero discards the remaining positive components whenever that term is non-zero but arbitrarily small.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the case split and the flawed \min formula with the standard continuity of the tangent cone projection map \tensX' \mapsto \proj_{\tangent_{\tensX'}\!\tensM_{\leq\vecr}}(-\nabla f(\tensX')) on the fixed-rank stratum \tensM_{\underline{\vecr}}, which directly ensures \|\tensV_{\tensX_{\underline{\vecr}}}\|_\frob \geq \frac{1}{2}\|\tensV_{\underline{\tensX}}\|_\frob > 0$ for all \tensX_{\underline{\vecr}} sufficiently close to \underline{\tensX}.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 4.4 fails to establish a strictly positive decrease \delta(\underline{\tensX}) > 0 in Case 3, leaving the global convergence guarantee in Theorem 4.5 unproven for accumulation points in \tensM_{\leq\vecr} \setminus (\tensM_\vecr \cup \tensM_{<\vecr}).
issues.title: Vanishing lower bound in Case 3 of Proposition 4.4
issues.why_classification: The primary claim that a positive decrease \delta(\underline{\tensX}) > 0 exists remains true; repairing it requires replacing the faulty explicit case split with a contained continuity argument on the smooth stratum \tensM_{\underline{\vecr}} without altering any algorithms or theorems.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider $\breve{\vecr}=( reve{r}_1,\breve{r}_2,\dots,\breve{r}_d)$ with $\breve{r}_k=\min\{r_k-1,\rank(\matx_{(k)})\}$ for $k\in I$ and $ reve{r}_k=r_k$ for $k\in[d]\setminus I$.

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 2 of Proposition 5.3, Algorithm 2 decreases the rank by at most 1 in each mode ($I_k = \{\rank-1, \rank\}$), so when $\underline{r}_k < r_k - 1$, the candidate $\tensX_{\breve{\vecr}}$ has strictly higher rank than $\underline{\tensX}$ (i.e. $\breve{r}_k > \underline{r}_k$). Because $\Span(\breve{\matu}_k)$ has strictly larger dimension than $\Span(\underline{\matu}_k)$, $\proj_{\breve{\matu}_k}^\perp$ projects onto a strictly smaller subspace than $\proj_{\underline{\matu}_k}^\perp$. As $\tensX_{\breve{\vecr}} \to \underline{\tensX}$, components of $\nabla f(\underline{\tensX})$ orthogonal to $\Span(\underline{\matu}_k)$ can fall into $\Span(\breve{\matu}_k)$ and be annihilated by $\proj_{\breve{\matu}_k}^\perp$. Hence $\|\tilde{\proj}_k(\nabla f(\tensX_{\breve{\vecr}}))\|_\frob$ can vanish as $\tensX_{\breve{\vecr}} \to \underline{\tensX}$ even when the limit at $\underline{\tensX}$ is non-zero (apocalypse). Thus $\|\tensV_{\tensX_{\breve{\vecr}}}\|_\frob$ is not bounded away from 0, Proposition 5.3 fails, and Theorem 5.4 is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must redesign Algorithm 2's rank-decreasing mechanism to consider lower-rank candidates all the way down to $\rank_\Delta(\matx_{(k)})$ (abandoning the single-singular-value check in (5.1) and Remark 5.1) so that the exact rank of $\underline{\tensX}$ is visited, or establish a new proof showing that sequences of single-rank drops avoid apocalypse.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition 5.3 is invalid, and Theorem 5.4's guarantee that all accumulation points of rfGRAP-R are stationary is unproven whenever the accumulation point has rank defect $\geq 2$.
issues.title: Invalid lower bound on tangent cone projection and failure of apocalypse-free property in rfGRAP-R
issues.why_classification: The advertised convergence guarantee of Algorithm 2 (Theorem 5.4) fails, and fixing it requires modifying the algorithm's definition and abandoning its key design feature (only checking the smallest singular value).
